newsitem.title: USA: Airline apologizes for Fidel Castro stunts.
newsitem.headline: Airline apologizes for Fidel Castro stunts.

text.p: American Airlines has apologised after passengers on its first Austin-to-Miami flight complained about jokes involving Cuban President Fidel Castro, the Miami Herald reported on Thursday.
"American Airlines regrets that our Austin employees -- in their enthusiasm for our new Miami service -- demonstrated a complete lack of sensitivity," the company said in a statement.

Staffers in Miami and at the Dallas headquarters of parent AMR Corp. were unaware of the "unfortunate incident," and executives were "appalled" when they learned of it, the statement, released on Wednesday, said.
An spokeswoman for the airline declined on Thursday to elaborate, but the newspaper said a Castro look-alike caused double takes at the gate of the first Austin-to-Miami flight on Sunday.
"I was so surprised that I shrieked," Cuban-American lawyer Ana Maria Pozo told the Herald. There was also a Carmen Miranda imitator, she added.
Once passengers were on board Flight 480, the pilot announced, "This is Fidel Castro, and I'm going to fly you to Miami."
Pozo said she suffered "an ugly emotional shock" and had told the crew the stunts were in bad taste and insulted all Cubans.

Castro is a reviled figure among Cuban exiles, about 800,000 of whom live in greater Miami. The Cuban president's communist revolution sent waves of refugees fleeing across the Florida Straits, many leaving behind families and property.
